Buttering difficulty (The Good Ride): Semi-Hard [30] CONSTRUCTION & MATERIALS 58. Core material: Super Fly II 700G Core — stronger and lighter woods in specific areas for pop, strength, reduced weight [32] 59. Core wood species: Dual-species wood core [25] 60. Core profiling: Squeezebox — thicker powerful sections combined with thinner flexible sections for energy transfer, snap, stability [33] 61. Core zones: Dualzone EGD — wood grain along heel and toe edge in two unbroken zones perpendicular to rest of core for consistent edge hold and strength [34] 62. Laminate: 45° Carbon Highlights — tip-to-tail carbon layer reducing weight; 45° angled fibres provide a more aggressive ride [35] 63. Carbon reinforcement: Full tip-to-tail carbon layer [35] 64. Base material: Sintered WFO — extra absorbent, high density sintered material infused with specially formulated wax [36] 65. Base type: Sintered (absorbs and holds wax better, faster performance, requires more frequent wax application) [37] 66. Resin: Super Sap Epoxy — bio-based resin, reduces carbon footprint by 50% over conventional petroleum-based epoxies [38] 67. Mounting system: The Channel — channel-based mounting for fine-tuned stance width/location, compatible with most binding brands [39] 68. Binding compatibility: Works best with Burton EST bindings; compatible with all major binding brands [40] 69. EST binding note: EST bindings are ONLY compatible with the Burton Channel system [41] 70. Tip/tail design: Pro-Tip — tip and tail taper at points, reducing swing weight and promoting mobility [42] 71. Factory ride preparation: Infinite Ride — boards overbuilt then broken down by machinery for consistent ride from day one to day 100 [43] 72. Factory tuning: Board comes waxed and ready for the mountain from the factory [44] SIZE-SPECIFIC SPECIFICATIONS (merchant-verified) 73. The Good Ride explicitly states this is "best for advanced experts only" and that "a committed intermediate will take some lumps." 81. Target rider (Burton blog): Riders chasing natural mountain flow and aggressive artistic expression [46] 82. Riding style (The Good Ride): Alternative Freeride [30] TERRAIN & RATINGS 83. Park rating: 5/10 [MERCHANT] 84. All mountain rating: 10/10 [MERCHANT] 85. Powder rating: 7/10 [MERCHANT] 86. Carving performance: Great [30] 89. Speed performance: Great [30] 90. Base glide: Good [30] 91. Uneven snow: Good [30] 92. Switch riding: Average [30] 93. Jumps: Good [30] 94. Jibbing: Poor [30] 95. Pipe: Average [30] 96. On snow feel: Semi-Locked In [30] 97. Turn initiation: Medium [30] 98. Skidded turns: Semi-Hard [30] 99. Edge hold: Medium Snow [30] 100. Approx. weight feel: Feels Normal [30] REVIEW OPINIONS & USER EXPERIENCE 101. Review positive (The Good Ride): Satisfying springy turn [11] 102. Review positive (The Good Ride): Seems like a decent floater in powder [11] 103. Review negative (The Good Ride): Edge lets go easy in harder snow [11] 104. Review summary (The Good Ride): Very satisfying turn in good conditions; more than just a board for hard turns; shorter, wider, more aggressive, stiffer, poppy shape that feels technical [30] 105. Review positive (King Snow/Aari): Super good edge hold; able to lay a trench in any turn style; super stable on groomers [48] 106. Review con (King Snow): May feel too aggressive or stiff for casual riders [49] 107. Snowboard Magazine award: Platinum Pick 2026 — "One of our favorite carving boards of the year" [10] 108. Review (Snowboard Mag): Incredibly versatile; nimble at lower speeds yet incredibly stable at high velocity [31] 109. Davey (big guy perspective, The Good Ride, 163 size): Board fit perfectly at 6'3.5", 245lbs, size 12 boot; felt edgeless/washy on harder snow in morning; chattery in hardpack; great once conditions softened [50] 110. Davey preference note: Personally liked the Burton Counterbalance better, but the Sketch Artist is still a fun board [50] 111. Forum opinion: Similar specs to the Big Gulp and Show Stopper; likely rides like "a super grippy twin fin on the mountain" [51] 112. Forum user experience (151 size): Great slower to moderate speed soul carver in good conditions; didn't float exceptionally well for 155lb rider [52] 113. Forum concern: Some consider the Sketch Artist too wide for smaller-booted riders (EU 40) [53] 114. Blog opinion (Find Your Haven Outdoors): Described as "the soul turner's dream deck" [54] 115. Burton's description: Most freestyle-friendly all-terrain board in the Family Tree line [27] EDGE HOLD DISAGREEMENT 116. Edge hold (King Snow/Aari review): "It held an edge super well" [48] — DISAGREEMENT with The Good Ride which rates edge hold as "Medium Snow" and notes it "lets go easy in harder snow" [11][30]. This could be attributable to different conditions, rider weight, and size ridden. BOOT SIZE RECOMMENDATIONS (The Good Ride) 117. 151 ideal US boot size: 8-10 [55] 118. 155 ideal US boot size: 8.5-10.5 [55] 119. 159 ideal US boot size: 10-12 [55] 120. 163 ideal US boot size: 11-13 [55] 121. Fits boot size (The Good Ride summary): US 8-10 and 10-12 [30] SUSTAINABILITY 122. Sustainability feature: Super Sap bio-based resin reduces carbon footprint by 50% vs petroleum-based epoxies [38] 123. Sustainability feature: Less oil consumption per board [56] MANUFACTURING 124. Manufacturer: Burton Snowboards, headquartered Burlington, Vermont, USA [57] 125. Manufacturing location (The Good Ride): Austria by The Mothership [30] 126. Manufacturing context: Burton moved production from Vermont to Austria in 2010; higher-end boards produced in Austria, others in China [58] 127. Burton founding: Founded by Jake Burton Carpenter in 1977 [57] 128. Burton B Corp status: Burton is a certified B Corporation [59] WARRANTY 129. Warranty: 3-year warranty from date of purchase for all 2014+ Burton snowboards with The Channel mounting system [21] COMPARABLE PRODUCTS & COMPETITORS 130. In-line comparison: Burton Family Tree Hometown Hero — directional camber, 12mm taper (vs 18mm), similar core/base tech, more rockered nose, slightly softer torsionally [60] 131. In-line comparison: Burton Counterbalance — preferred by The Good Ride's Davey over the Sketch Artist [50] 132. In-line comparison: Burton Custom — traditional camber all-mountain directional twin, less taper, more switch-friendly [61] 133. In-line comparison: Burton Family Tree High Fidelity — aggressive freeride, 7mm taper, 25mm setback [62] 134. Similar boards (The Good Ride): Jones Hovercraft, Gnu Gremlin, Korua Transition Finder, Salomon Dancehaul, K2 Excavator, Jones Mind Expander, YES PYL Uninc [30] 135. Competition: Salomon Dancehaul — noted as having better edge hold than both Burton Hometown Hero and Custom in one forum comparison [63] BRAND REPUTATION 136. Brand reputation: Burton is one of the longest-standing pillars of snowboarding; innovating for over 40 years [64] 137. Brand market position: Largest snowboard manufacturer in the world; products marketed in over 4,348 stores worldwide [57] 138. evo reputation: Major US specialty retailer; 5% price-match guarantee; up to 1-year return policy [15] 139. REI reputation: Trusted US outdoor cooperative retailer [13] 140. Darkside Snowboards reputation: Established 1989, Vermont-based specialist retailer [16] 141. Blauer Board Shop reputation: Rated as "Favorite Store" by The Good Ride review site [14] ADDITIONAL TECHNICAL NOTES 142. Progressive sidecut description: Sidecut tightens near the tail for energetic exits and responsive edge hold [26] 143. Directional flex description: Stiffer tail concentrates pop; stiffer nose for control [MERCHANT] 144. Channel replaced Burton's 3D mounting pattern in 2014, featuring two parallel slots along the snowboard edges [23] 145. Channel allows nearly infinite mounting options using just two screws per binding [23] 146. Carbon highlights 45° vs 60°: A 45° fiber angle provides a more aggressive ride; 60° creates a more maneuverable/playful feel [35] 147. Sintered WFO base requires more frequent waxing than extruded bases [37] 148. Camber has been the dominant board bend in the snowboard industry for almost 40 years [65]
